title: Hear-No-Evil Monkey Emoji 🙉 Meaning: Not Listening
description: The hear-no-evil monkey emoji 🙉 covers its ears. It means not wanting to hear something: spoilers, TMI, gossip or criticism. See usage, examples and FAQs.
summary: The 🙉 hear-no-evil monkey emoji shows a monkey with its hands over its ears. It means 'I don't want to hear this' or 'I'm not listening.' People use it to dodge spoilers, too much information, bad news, and unwanted advice, usually in a joking way.
meaning: Of the three wise monkeys, this is the one that says 'la la la.' Covering your ears is a childish, obvious way to refuse information, and 🙉 carries that playful stubbornness. It shows up when a friend starts describing last night's episode, when a sibling overshares about their love life, or when someone is about to say 'I told you so.' The sender is not really offended; they are theatrically opting out.

A second use is about volume. People send it for anything too loud: a concert, a neighbor's drill, a baby on a plane, a karaoke performance that should not have happened. In this case the monkey is protecting its ears, not its innocence. Its wide-open eyes and mouth also give it a startled look, so some use it for 'did I just hear that?', a reaction to a shocking remark.

The proverb behind it, 'hear no evil,' is represented at the Toshogu shrine in Nikko, Japan, by a carved monkey called Kikazaru. In that tradition, the gesture is about refusing to listen to wickedness. The emoji keeps a trace of this when used for avoiding gossip or staying out of drama, and it can also describe willful ignorance, such as a person who will not hear criticism.

contexts.label: In texting
contexts.body: It is a quick way to cut off a topic: 'no spoilers 🙉' or 'I don't need the details 🙉.' The mood is teasing. It also marks denial about something you would rather not face, like a bank balance after a holiday or the number of hours until the alarm rings.

contexts.label: On social media
contexts.body: Fans post 🙉 during premieres and finals to tell followers they are avoiding results. It appears under loud or chaotic videos, and in replies that jokingly refuse to accept an opinion. Parents use it for noisy households, and music lovers for a volume they both regret and enjoy.

contexts.label: In arguments
contexts.body: Aimed at another person, 🙉 accuses them of refusing to listen. Aimed at oneself, it says 'I'm not engaging with this.' Either way it can come across as dismissive, so it is better suited to friendly bickering than to a disagreement that needs resolving.

examples.text: Don't tell me who won, I'm watching tonight 🙉
Okay that's enough detail about your date 🙉
examples.meaning: Jokingly declaring the story is too much information.

examples.text: The upstairs neighbors got a drum kit 🙉
My dentist said I need to floss more 🙉
examples.meaning: Playfully refusing to accept good advice.

combos.meaning: The three wise monkeys together: staying out of trouble or refusing to engage with drama.
Music that is too loud, or tuning someone out with a song.
A firm no-spoilers or not-listening signal.

confusedWith.difference: 🙈 hides its eyes and usually signals shyness or embarrassment. 🙉 blocks its ears and is about rejecting information or noise. The first is bashful, the second is stubborn or overwhelmed.
🙊 covers its mouth to show the sender said too much or is keeping a secret. 🙉 concerns what comes in, not what goes out: it refuses to listen.
👂 means the opposite: listening closely, eavesdropping, or 'I'm all ears.' 🙉 shuts sound out. Deaf and hard-of-hearing topics are better represented by 🧏 or 🦻 than by either.

avoid: Do not send it when someone is trying to raise a real concern with you, because it tells them their words do not matter.
Avoid using it to refer to deafness or hearing loss, which it does not represent and which can offend.
Never use monkey emojis to refer to a person's race; that is a racist use.
design: The glyph is a brown monkey's face, seen from the front, with a hand pressed over each ear. Its eyes are open and round and the mouth is usually open in a small 'o,' giving it a surprised look. Vendors differ in fur tone and facial detail but agree on the pose.

faqs.q: What does 🙉 mean from a girl or a guy?
faqs.a: They are jokingly refusing to hear something: a spoiler, a criticism, an awkward detail. It can also mean something was loud or shocking. It is not a flirting emoji, though it appears in playful teasing.
In banter, no. During a serious conversation it can be, since it mimics plugging your ears while someone talks. Tone and timing decide whether it is funny or dismissive.

faqs.q: What is the name of the hear-no-evil monkey?
faqs.a: In the Japanese tradition it is Kikazaru. Its companions are Mizaru, who covers his eyes, and Iwazaru, who covers his mouth. All three have been in Unicode since 2010.
The trio represents the saying 'see no evil, hear no evil, speak no evil.' In messages it means staying out of something, keeping quiet about what you know, or playing innocent.
